stages.request: `Decision.retry_after` is a float number of seconds, and our dashboards end up showing values like 0.30000000000000004. Please make it a whole number of milliseconds instead, rounded up so a client that waits that long is never early: a wait of a third of a second should come back as 334. It stays 0 when the hit is allowed.

Building a `TokenBucket` by hand means working out tokens per second, which nobody gets right for slow rates. Change the constructor to `TokenBucket(capacity, refill_period, clock)`, where `refill_period` is the number of seconds an empty bucket takes to refill to full capacity, so `TokenBucket(10, 60, clock)` gains one token every 6 seconds. A `refill_period` of zero or less should raise `ValueError: refill_period must be positive: <value>`.

Bug: on a key whose policy is `10/minute`, `throttle.check('upload', cost=15)` raises RateLimitExceeded telling the client to retry in under a minute, and a token bucket hands out a wait as well, but that hit can never succeed, so our clients retry forever. On a sliding window the same call crashes with IndexError. A hit costing more than the limit (a bucket's capacity) should be refused straight away with `ValueError: cost 15 exceeds limit 10`, from both `hit()` and `check()`, without spending anything.

The `reset_in` field that limiters report from `state()` is relative to the moment it was read, so two snapshots taken a few seconds apart can't be lined up. Replace it with `reset_at`: the clock time at which the limiter will be full again, or the current time if it already is.

We want to pass Python's `time` module straight in as the clock. Read the current time by calling `clock.monotonic()` rather than `clock.now()`, and have `ManualClock` provide `monotonic()` in place of `now()` so there is only one spelling.

Busy services hit the 1000-key cap and lose the limits of keys that are still active. Raise the default `max_keys` to 10000, and have `summarise()` also report `evicted`: how many keys the throttle has evicted to stay under its cap since it was created.
